question.text: Narmada PE Fund's investee Chola Retail has: Enterprise Value from DCF = INR 5,000 crore; Long-term debt = INR 800 crore; Preference capital = INR 150 crore; Cash & equivalents = INR 50 crore. What is the equity value?

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity Value = EV - (Debt - Cash) - Preference Capital = 5,000 - (800 - 50) - 150 = 5,000 - 750 - 150 = INR 4,100 crore. The PDF Illustration 11.3 uses the bridge: EV = Equity + Net Debt + Preference. Rearranging: Equity = EV - Net Debt - Preference. The Trap: INR 4,200 forgets to subtract preference capital; INR 5,000 ignores the entire bridge; INR 3,950 double-counts cash. Always net cash against debt before subtracting. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the identical bridge. XXI-B (PM) uses it in DCF-based stock picking. XV (Research Analyst) tests 'minority interest' as an additional item (EV - Debt + Cash - Minority Int - Preference = Equity). Manager's Pro-Tip: In Cat II PE buyouts, preference capital is often CCPS held by existing VCs — be explicit in your SPA about whether the preference coupon (and conversion ratchet) is included in your EV-to-equity bridge, or you will under-pay founders.
